title: Equal scalar defects split the tensor product with an opposite algebra
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S$ its separable closure, and $A,B$ finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebras. Let $x,y$ belong to the second continuous Galois cohomology of $S^\times$ [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology], with its natural Galois action and discrete coefficient topology. Suppose $R(A,x)$ and $R(B,y)$ are scalar-defect realizations [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect] and $x=y$. Then there exists an integer $n>0$ and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_K B^{\mathrm{op}}\cong M_n(K)$.

proof.text: Apply exists_tensor_opposite_scalarDefect_lifts to retain n≠0, the tensor splitting e, locally constant b, and actual cocycles z,w with their class projection and quotient-defect equations.
Compose the two projection equations with x=y and obtain a locally constant scalar cochain a from exists_scalar_cochain_of_galoisUnits_class_eq.

Define b′(g)=scalar(a(g) inverse)*b(g). Local constancy is preserved by composition and multiplication. Use centrality of scalar matrices and the quotient-defect identity to prove b′(g)g(b′(h))=b′(gh), cancelling a(g), g(a(h)), and a(gh). Scalar matrices commute with each e(1 tensor d), so their inverse pair cancels and the original conjugation equation is unchanged. These are explicit Lean calculations, not new hypotheses.
Apply nonempty_algEquiv_matrix_of_galois_cocycle to D=A tensor Bop, e and the genuine cocycle b′; pair the resulting K-algebra equivalence with n and n≠0.
